text:
maya: Heads up — us-west-2-rt cluster showing sustained queue depth ~480, GPUs at ~96% mem, saw 3 inference pods OOM and tail latency jumped to ~1.8s around 09:12 UTC.
ben: Is this dedicated or hosted capacity? any recent deploys?
maya: Hosted pool (rt tier). No deploys in the last hour, looks like a large incoming burst from a partner integration.
sam: Can you paste the scheduler log snippet?
maya: here are the top lines:
```
2026-03-18T09:11:58Z scale-decider: candidates=8 healthy=6 warm=5 targetUtil=0.91
2026-03-18T09:12:03Z admission: queue=482 inflight=124 admitted=78 reject=0
2026-03-18T09:12:11Z pod/inf-rt-7 OOMKilled
2026-03-18T09:12:14Z tail-latency.p95=1800ms
```
irene: Looks like warm pool underprovisioned for the new traffic pattern. We need to reduce cold starts and increase spare capacity.
ben: Current warmpool config for rt in us-west-2: ```yaml
warmPool:
  minReady: 4
  scaleUpBurst: 3
autoscaler:
  targetUtilization: 0.75
  scaleOutCooldown: 30s
  scaleInCooldown: 2m
```
sam: Two levers: (A) raise minReady to avoid hitting cold scale-out on bursts (cost up), (B) tighten admission control so we don't OOM by accepting too many inflight heavy requests.
maya: Proposal: bump minReady -> 10, scaleOutCooldown -> 15s, scaleInCooldown -> 5m, and add a token-bucket admission cap per cluster to smooth bursts.
irene: Also consider model-level priority tags: route low-priority async requests to a cheaper quantized variant when queue>200.
ben: Agree. For token-bucket idea: refillRate = sum(GPU_tokens) * 0.85, bucketSize = 1.5 * expected_concurrency. That lets short bursts pass but prevents sustained overload.
ops-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0318-rt-surge. Assigned: sam, ben.
sam: I'll sketch the admission rule patch: pseudocode:
```
if cluster_util > 0.9 {
  admission.allow_priority('high')
  admission.throttle_priority('default', rate=refillRate*0.4)
  admission.reject('low')
}
```
maya: Cost tradeoff: 6 extra warm GPUs in us-west-2 adds ~$9k/mo. If it prevents OOMs and client SLA hits, likely worth it.
irene: We should target region-level spare capacity instead of per-pool hard numbers. Suggest policy: maintain spare_capacity = max(ceil(0.1*total_capacity), 6) per region.
ben: Action items: 1) Sam to deploy admission throttle canary to us-west-2-rt (2h canary) — due in 30m. 2) Maya to patch warmPool.minReady -> 10 and scaleInCooldown -> 5m, scheduled as config rollout this evening. 3) Irene to add model-routing fallback for low-priority requests when queue>200.
maya: I'll also temporarily raise the cluster-level rejection_threshold to 480 so admission starts earlier rather than after OOMs.
sam: Canary patch ready, will POST canary and monitor p95/p99 and OOMs.
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: us-west-2-rt/admission-throttle v1.1 -> 09:45 UTC (canary-size=12%).
ben: Monitoring: add a dashboard panel for "warmpool spare" and "admission token utilization" and an alert when token_util < 0.15 for >2m.
ops-bot: Reminder: tag incident updates in INC-2026-0318-rt-surge thread.
maya: Thanks — will update after canary.
ben: If canary looks good, we should also consider an automated policy: when weekly rolling forecast predicts >50% probability of >2x baseline burst in next 24h, pre-warm + create temporary reservation.
irene: Good idea. For now, prioritize the 3 action items and a 4-hr postmortem once stable.
sam: Starting canary in 3m.
maya: Update 09:58 UTC: canary up, initial token_util at 0.6, queue dropped to ~120, no new OOMs so far.
ben: Nice. Leave canary running for 2 hours and then decide on full rollout.
deploy-bot: Canary status: healthy -> will auto-promote if 2h stable.
maya: Closing loop later with metrics. Thanks team :)
